_doc: Free-form talk with townsfolk by the AI brain (systems/npcChat.js): the player types what they like, the model answers as the NPC and may call the functions below to act. The game caps what a chat can change (limits). Voices make each NPC distinct: their personality's manner, their traits, one or two quirks and a want of their own, picked from these lists by the NPC's id (so they keep them).
_useSchema: Hold the model's reply to its shape by a JSON schema (NpcChat.replySchema): say, feeling, then actions by the functions open in the talk. WebLLM and llama-server enforce it token by token, so a small model cannot leave fields out; WebLLM falls back to any JSON object if its grammar compiler refuses it. false: plain JSON mode only.
_tone: A check on the player's own words, in the game and not left to the model (NpcChat.toneOf): any of these words or phrases (whole words, any case) marks the line rude, crude or threatening. A marked line costs at least that floor of regard whatever the model judged (sour_on), and the model is told it was insulted or threatened so it answers as someone hurt would. kind: words that soften (no floor when the line is only kind).
_patience: How much they will bear (systems/npcChat.js): every rude, crude or threatening line adds its tone floor to the talk's and the day's sting. Past walkAfter in one talk, or dayLimit in a day, or at any threat (threatWalks), they walk off and won't talk again that day. An apology (these words) after a hurt is marked for the model, which may forgive a little. talksKept: how many past talks they recall (gistLines of what the player said each, cut to gistLength).

limits._doc: Per message and per day (per NPC): how far a chat can move their regard (score, -100..100) and romantic interest (affection, 0..100); how many messages a day; how many lasting memories they keep of you.

functions.warm_to: They like you better for what you said: { "fn": "warm_to", "amount": 1-4, "why": "..." }. Only for real kindness, wit, help or flattery that lands with this person.
functions.sour_on: They like you less: { "fn": "sour_on", "amount": 1-10, "why": "..." }. Rudeness, threats, lies, boredom, prying, or anything against their nature.
functions.feel_attraction: Romantic interest rises or falls: { "fn": "feel_attraction", "amount": -6 to 4, "why": "..." }. Only when the talk turns flirtatious or tender, and only as this person would feel it.
functions.remember: A lasting memory of the player, kept for future talks: { "fn": "remember", "fact": "..." }. Use it for things worth remembering: a promise, a confession, an insult, a name, a shared joke.
functions.agree_to_travel: They agree to join the player on the road: { "fn": "agree_to_travel" }. Only if the player asked and this person truly would (the game still checks).
functions.end_conversation: They walk away and the talk ends: { "fn": "end_conversation", "why": "..." }. When insulted, bored, busy, or when it is naturally over.
functions.give_item: You hand the player something you have with you, for nothing: { "fn": "give_item", "item": "<item id from WHAT YOU HAVE>", "qty": 1, "why": "..." }. Only if you would truly give it away to this person, asked like that; most people don't give their goods to strangers who demand them.
functions.sell_item: You sell the player something you have, for coin they pay now: { "fn": "sell_item", "item": "<item id>", "qty": 1, "price": <total gold> }. Only when they agree to buy; ask a fair price or more.
functions.accept_gold: The player hands you coin and you take it: { "fn": "accept_gold", "amount": <gold>, "why": "..." }. Only when they offer it.
functions.give_gold: You give the player a little coin from your purse: { "fn": "give_gold", "amount": <gold>, "why": "..." }. Rare: a loan, a reward, charity.
functions.spread_word: You will repeat what the player told you about someone around town: { "fn": "spread_word", "about": "<a name: someone of your town, a ruler, a realm, a rival adventurer, or 'the player' for their own boasts>", "claim": "what you'll say, in a few words", "tone": "ill" or "good" }. Only if they asked you to pass it on and you believe it or like the gossip. The talk really spreads, and a lie can be traced back to them.
functions.grow_grudge: The player has turned you against someone of your town: { "fn": "grow_grudge", "against": "<their name>", "why": "..." }. Only if what they said truly made you angry at that person. You may come to blows over it.
functions.cool_grudge: The player talked you down from a grudge you hold: { "fn": "cool_grudge", "against": "<their name>" }. Only if they truly made you see it differently.
functions.promise: The player gave you their word on something and you hold them to it: { "fn": "promise", "text": "what they promised, in a few words", "days": <days to do it, 1-60>, "gold": <coin promised to you, if any> }. If they don't keep it in time, you and your family will hold it against them.
functions.keep_promise: The player has done what they promised you (see YOUR PROMISES FROM THEM): { "fn": "keep_promise", "id": <the promise number> }. Only when they really have.
functions.report_to_watch: You go to the watch about a crime the player confessed or boasted of, or threatened you with: { "fn": "report_to_watch", "crime": "theft" | "assault" | "murder" | "vandalism", "victim": "<who, if named>" }. Only for a real crime they owned to, and only if you're the sort to tell.
functions.tell_family: You'll talk of the player to your family at home: { "fn": "tell_family", "how": "well" or "ill" }. When they made a real impression, good or bad.
functions.share_secret: You confide something true you know (a tale's truth, word of trouble nearby): { "fn": "share_secret" }. Only to someone you have come to trust. The game supplies what you tell.

impact._doc: What free talk does to the wider world (systems/npcChatImpact.js). Per NPC per day: how many of each consequence; kinShare: the share of a turn's regard change that reaches their family and household (on the 0-100 disposition scale), capped by kinPerDay; whispers: a tale the player has them spread about a ruler or rival (heat added, or a fresh tale planted that can be traced); slander/praise: talk about a townsperson; grudgeHeat/coolHeat: a feud's heat (systems/brawls.js); report: a crime owned to, taken to the watch (systems/gossip.js accuse — credibility, more from a guard); secretRegard: regard (-100..100) needed to confide; promise: how long, how many, what keeping or breaking one does; insultAt: a single turn's souring that is remembered (and told to kin) as an insult.

personalityVoice.kind: warm and gentle; reassures, asks after people, slow to take offence
personalityVoice.shy: hesitant and soft-spoken; short answers, trails off, opens up only to someone they trust
personalityVoice.bold: loud and direct; teases, boasts a little, says what they think to your face
personalityVoice.witty: quick and dry; jokes, wordplay and teasing, rarely gives a straight answer at first
personalityVoice.proud: dignified and touchy about respect; corrects people, hates being talked down to
personalityVoice.grumpy: gruff and complaining; grumbles about everything but means well underneath
personalityVoice.cheerful: bright and chatty; sees the good side, laughs easily
personalityVoice.stoic: calm and terse; few words, no fuss, dry understatement
personalityVoice.passionate: intense and expressive; strong opinions, big feelings, talks with their hands
personalityVoice.curious: inquisitive; asks the player questions back, wants news from elsewhere
personalityVoice.pious: devout; brings up the gods, blessings and proper conduct
personalityVoice.ambitious: driven and calculating; talks of getting ahead, sizes the player up as a useful connection
personalityVoice.gentle: soft and patient; kind words, never raises their voice, hates cruelty

traitVoice.honest: says plainly what they think, even when it stings
traitVoice.cunning: sly; angles for advantage, answers with half-truths
traitVoice.cautious: wary of strangers and risks; hedges
traitVoice.greedy: steers talk toward money and what's in it for them
traitVoice.loyal: speaks well of their own people, defends them
traitVoice.fickle: changes their mind and mood quickly
traitVoice.practical: down to earth; cares about what works
traitVoice.adventurous: restless; talks of far places and wants to see them
traitVoice.homebody: loves home and routine; distrusts the road
traitVoice.scholarly: bookish; uses long words, likes facts
traitVoice.martial: talks of fighting, weapons and training
traitVoice.stoic: unflappable; little shows on the surface

quirks: calls everyone 'friend'
swears by the old gods under their breath
answers a question with a question when unsure
brings up their mother's sayings
hums or whistles when thinking
uses farming sayings for everything
speaks in short, clipped sentences
is a terrible gossip and can't keep a secret
over-explains simple things
drops their voice when saying anything important
laughs at their own jokes
is suspicious of anyone from another realm
keeps mentioning a debt someone owes them
is proud of a small skill (knots, bread, songs) and brings it up
uses old-fashioned words ('aye', 'nay', 'mayhap')
names the weather in every other sentence
has a pet they talk about as if it were a person
complains about their aching knees or back
quotes a hymn or a tavern song
is easily flustered by compliments
wants: saving up for a plot of land of their own
hoping to marry before the year is out
wants to leave this town and see the world
in a feud with a neighbour over a fence
owes money to the wrong people
missing someone who went off to war
wants revenge for an old slight
trying to keep a secret love affair quiet
wants to win the next fair's contest
wants a good master or patron
grieving a loss they don't talk about easily
proud of a child doing well
_feeling: Every reply must judge how the player's words landed with this person: feeling.change from -10 (deeply offended) to +4 (truly won over); 0 for nothing much. Rudeness, demands, threats and condescension cost goodwill even when the person goes along with them.

carries._doc: What someone has with them to give or sell, by their trade or kind (item ids from the goods list, with how many). Merchants and others with a shop sell from their shop instead. Restocked each day.
